scope: Two read-only delegated primary-literature searches for the C8 openness gate. No file edits or scientific verification runs were delegated.
earlier_source_audit:
## Assessment

**No accessible source read settles the exact C8 covariance classification. This does not certify novelty or historical openness.** Earlier literature contains genuine restricted classification results—not merely sufficient constructions—and established nonfactorized invariant-polarization examples.

“Partly” below means overlap with a construction or structural result, **not** anticipation of the complete four-LG-mode theorem.

| Source / access | Exact scope, locator, short quotation | Relation to C8; settles? |
|---|---|---|
| **Massimo Santarsiero, “Polarization invariance in a Young interferometer” (2007), JOSA A 24, 3493–3499.** DOI [10.1364/JOSAA.24.003493](https://doi.org/10.1364/JOSAA.24.003493). [Author-hosted full text](http://webusers.fis.uniroma3.it/~ottica/sant/pubs/Max097.pdf) **read**. | **§3, Eqs. (14)–(20):** assumes proportional polarization matrices at two pinholes. Requiring the **entire normalized polarization matrix**, not only its degree, to remain identical across the interference pattern forces the 4×4 covariance to factorize as a scalar-source matrix tensor a polarization matrix. Quote: “the 4 × 4 correlation matrix representing the two-point source at the pinholes consists of four blocks proportional to one another”. | **Partly.** An actual covariance characterization under stated assumptions. Its observable is stronger than constant \(P\), its inputs are restricted, and its probes are Young-interference phases. It does not classify C8’s two-radial-order covariance sum or its nonproduct branches. |
| **M. Santarsiero, V. Ramírez-Sánchez, R. Borghi, “Partially correlated thin annular sources: the vectorial case” (2010), JOSA A 27, 1450–1456.** DOI [10.1364/JOSAA.27.001450](https://doi.org/10.1364/JOSAA.27.001450). [Author manuscript](http://webusers.fis.uniroma3.it/~ottica/sant/pubs/Max110.pdf) **read**. | Infinitely thin annular sources, angularly shift-invariant 2×2 BCP matrix. **§2, Eqs. (3)–(13):** Fourier-block PSD realizability and modal decomposition; **§3, Eq. (28):** propagated local matrix is a Bessel-intensity-weighted sum of Fourier blocks. **§4, Eqs. (33)–(36):** opposite angular harmonics and counter-rotating circular polarizations, mutually uncorrelated with unequal powers, give arbitrary uniform degree and unchanged polarization. Quote: “at any distance z, at any point of the transverse plane.” | **Partly—important construction-level prior art.** Opposite-order degeneracy already yields nonfactorized invariant sources. These are annular/Bessel fields, not the finite common-waist LG space; no classification of all constant-\(P\) covariances is given. |
| **V. Ramírez-Sánchez, G. Piquero, M. Santarsiero, “Synthesis and characterization of partially coherent beams with propagation-invariant transverse polarization pattern” (2010), Optics Communications 283, 4484–4489.** DOI [10.1016/j.optcom.2010.04.081](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.optcom.2010.04.081). [Author manuscript](http://webusers.fis.uniroma3.it/~ottica/sant/pubs/Max109.pdf) **read**. | **§II, Eqs. (2)–(8):** arbitrary radial scalar CSD multiplied by the outer product of azimuthal/spiral Jones vectors. It explicitly attributes a necessary-and-sufficient azimuthal-polarization condition to Tervo (2003), and its spiral extension to Gori (2008). **§III, Eqs. (9)–(10):** synthesis through radial coherent components. Quote: “must present perfect correlation between points belonging to circles ρ = constant.” | **No.** A restricted, locally fully polarized (\(P=1\)) invariant-pattern class, experimentally synthesized. It is not a classification of arbitrary partially polarized C8 covariances. The original Tervo/Gori proofs were not available in full text here. |
| **R. Martínez-Herrero, D. Maluenda, G. Piquero, J. C. González de Sande, M. Santarsiero, F. Gori, “Partially polarized pseudo-Schell model sources” (2017), SPIE 10453, 104531N.** DOI [10.1117/12.2272154](https://doi.org/10.1117/12.2272154). [UCM full text](https://docta.ucm.es/bitstreams/ac596c3d-540d-471a-b3e0-ffef9007e85d/download) **read**. | **§3, Eqs. (8)–(15):** general matrix-valued radial-difference construction; worked example chooses diagonal \(H\), giving one scalar CSD times a fixed diagonal polarization matrix. **§4, Eq. (17):** radial envelope with vortex phase \(e^{im\theta}\); scalar Fresnel propagation preserves its polarization. Quote: “For the simple example developed in this work, the polarization properties of the source remain invariant in propagation.” | **Partly.** Established arbitrary constant-\(P\), partially coherent vortex construction of product form. The paper explicitly treats a particular example, not necessity or all admissible covariances. |
| **J. C. González de Sande, G. Piquero, J. C. Suárez-Bermejo, M. Santarsiero, “Mueller Matrix Polarimetry with Invariant Polarization Pattern Beams” (2021), Photonics 8, 491.** DOI [10.3390/photonics8110491](https://doi.org/10.3390/photonics8110491). [UPM full text](https://oa.upm.es/85952/1/9901073.pdf) **read**. | Perfectly coherent, nonuniformly **totally polarized** fields. **§2, Eqs. (2)–(5):** common waist and common Gouy index \(N=2p+|s|\) provide shape-invariant intensity and polarization. Includes \(LG_{0,\pm1}\). **§3, Eq. (11):** differences \(4j\) suffice for far-field recurrence only. Quote: “with one and the same value of N.” | **No.** Equal-mode-order sufficient construction for an invariant **state pattern**, up to transverse scaling. C8 allows two different radial orders and only fixes \(P\); this is not its covariance classification. |
| **R. Martínez-Herrero, G. Piquero, M. Santarsiero, F. Gori, J. C. González de Sande, “A class of vectorial pseudo-Schell model sources with structured coherence and polarization” (2022), Optics & Laser Technology 152, 108079.** DOI [10.1016/j.optlastec.2022.108079](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.optlastec.2022.108079). [UPM full text](https://oa.upm.es/87042/1/9906481.pdf) **read**. | **Eqs. (20)–(21):** radial scalar CSD times a prescribed angular matrix built from \(\cos\theta,\cos(\theta-\alpha)\), with correlation \(|b|\le1\). **Eq. (25):** generally angularly varying local \(P\). **§5, Eq. (33):** unchanged angular matrix after Fresnel propagation. Quote: “both the pattern of the polarization state and the degree of polarization remain unchanged during propagation.” | **No.** Establishes an invariant-pattern source family; usually \(P\) is not spatially constant. Special constant-\(P\) parameter choices do not constitute the arbitrary four-mode PSD classification. |
| **Franco Gori, “Partially correlated sources with complete polarization” (2008), Optics Letters 33, 2818–2820.** DOI [10.1364/OL.33.002818](https://doi.org/10.1364/OL.33.002818). [Primary abstract via PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19037437/) **read; full text inaccessible**. | Abstract states a universal correlation-matrix form for completely polarized planar sources, reducing realizability and vector modes to scalar problems; propagation-preserving cases are discussed. Quote: “any electromagnetic planar source endowed with complete polarization must be of a universal form”. No original equation locator established. | **No exact C8 settlement established.** Important \(P=1\) structural predecessor; cannot infer its complete propagation theorem from the abstract. |
| **Olga Korotkova, “Sufficient condition for polarization invariance of beams generated by quasi-homogeneous sources” (2011), Optics Letters 36, 3768–3770.** DOI [10.1364/OL.36.003768](https://doi.org/10.1364/OL.36.003768). [Primary abstract via PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21964091/) **read; full text inaccessible**. | Electromagnetic **quasi-homogeneous** sources; degree/state invariance **in the far zone**, with a Bessel-correlated example. Quote: “beams radiated by electromagnetic quasi-homogeneous sources into the far-zone”. Equation conditions not independently inspected. | **No.** Explicitly sufficient and far-zone-scoped, unlike C8’s necessary-and-sufficient all-forward-distance statement. |

### Inaccessible originals / important exclusions

- **Gori 2008** and **Korotkova 2011**, above: Optica CAPTCHA; no full-text repository location found.
- **Martínez-Herrero–Mejías 2007**, *Electromagnetic fields that remain totally polarized under propagation*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.optcom.2007.07.002): publisher 403; OpenAlex and UCM searches did not supply full text. Its exact theorem remains unassessed.
- **Tervo 2003**, *Azimuthal polarization and partial coherence*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1364/JOSAA.20.001974): [abstract read](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14570112/); original proof inaccessible.
- **Wolf 2007**, *Polarization invariance in beam propagation*, [abstract read](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18059946/): explicitly **sufficiency conditions**, matching source-plane and far-zone degree; no full text.
- **Korotkova–Wolf 2005**, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.optcom.2004.10.078): [institutional abstract read](https://stars.library.ucf.edu/facultybib2000/5363/), not full text.
- **Wu–Wang–Cai 2012**, [abstract read](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23263065/): explicitly says **degree varies** while the polarized part’s **state remains invariant**. This must not be counted as constant-degree prior art.
- Yajun Li (2015) deliberately excluded as assigned.

**Openness:** No current primary statement identifying the exact remaining C8 classification as open was located. The 2010 paper’s broad “derive the conditions” motivation is neither current nor specific enough. **Neither novelty nor historical openness is cleared by this audit.**
recent_optical_channel_audit:
## Gate conclusion

**No source read here establishes the complete C8 classification. No current primary statement explicitly calling the exact four-mode, arbitrary PSD-sector question open was located.** Therefore this audit neither clears novelty nor certifies historical openness.

The strongest crossover is **Ornelas et al. (2025)**: LG spatial projections, isotropic mixed-state noise, and constant-radius polarization-sphere geometry occur together. It is a construction/topological-resilience result—not the all-forward-Fresnel necessity theorem, radial \(n=0,1\) analysis, or unrestricted PSD-split classification.

## Primary-source evidence rows

| Source / access | Exact scope, locator, short quotation | Relation to C8; settles? |
|---|---|---|
| **“Encoding Higher-Order Polarization States into Robust Partially Coherent Optical Beams” — Zhen Dong, Yahong Chen, Fei Wang, Yangjian Cai, Ari T. Friberg, Tero Setälä (2022).** DOI **10.1103/PhysRevApplied.18.034036**. **Primary fulltext read:** [UEF accepted manuscript](https://erepo.uef.fi/bitstreams/7281a40a-e4a6-44af-9af8-a9f02d6bfb0a/download). | §II, Eqs. (1)–(2): coherent \(LG_{0,\pm\ell}\) higher-order-Poincaré construction. §III.A–B, Eqs. (6)–(14), Figs. 7–9: continuous coherence-engineered secondary source, with polarization reconstructed near focus/far field. Quote: **“We will show later that upon propagation the beam becomes more polarized”**. | **No.** Its principal partially coherent example changes local \(P\) with propagation; far-field recovery is not invariance everywhere. No arbitrary four-mode covariance necessity. Its “global degree” is polarized power fraction, not automatically the DoP of spatially integrated Stokes parameters. |
| **“Unified matrix representation for spin and orbital angular momentum in partially coherent beams” — Olga Korotkova, Greg Gbur (2021).** DOI **10.1103/PhysRevA.103.023529**. **Primary fulltext read:** [arXiv:2012.01332](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.01332). | §§III–VI: general COAM matrix, positivity and paraxial radial propagation; §IX.D, Eqs. (68)–(72): incoherent sum of two \(p=0,\ell=\pm1\) LG Schell-model beams; §X, Eqs. (81)–(89): full polarization–OAM correlation matrix. Quote: **“In free space, the elements of the COAM matrix can be propagated independently”**. | **Partly—representation/propagation background only.** It accommodates arbitrary radial coherence and polarization/OAM correlations, but does not classify constant local \(P\), derive the C8 radial-probe image, or impose a normal form on the sector sum. Its OAM purity is not local polarization purity. |
| **“Beams with propagation-invariant transverse polarization pattern” — J. C. G. de Sande, Gemma Piquero, Juan Carlos Suárez-Bermejo, Massimo Santarsiero (2021 preprint).** DOI **10.48550/arXiv.2102.00024**. **Primary fulltext read:** [arXiv PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.00024). | pp. 2–3, Eqs. (2)–(5): common-waist Gaussian-mode expansions; sufficient equal-order \(N=2p+|s|\) condition. p. 5: weaker far-field condition, orders differing by multiples of four. Quote: **“Here we are interested to perfectly polarized and perfectly coherent fields.”** | **No.** Shape-invariant polarization patterns of deterministic fields, not partially polarized covariance classification. Equal-Gouy-order constructions do not address interference between C8’s two distinct radial orders. |
| **“Gouy-phase-mediated propagation variations and revivals of transverse structure in vectorially structured light” — Ru-Yue Zhong, Zhi-Han Zhu, Hai-Jun Wu, Carmelo Rosales-Guzmán, Shu-Wei Song, Bao-Sen Shi (2021).** DOI **10.1103/PhysRevA.103.053520**. **Primary fulltext read:** [arXiv:2103.10887](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.10887). | §II, Eqs. (1), (3)–(4): deterministic two-polarization superposition; relative phase \(\Delta N\arctan(z/z_R)\). §III, Eqs. (7)–(10): same-order examples and different-radial-order revivals. Quote: **“in this study we only consider monochromatic waves”**. | **Partly—explicit radial/Gouy bridge, but no mixed-state channel classification.** Studies polarization orientation/ellipticity and profile revivals; these must not be equated with classification of constant partially polarized local \(P\). |
| **“On the overall polarisation properties of Poincaré beams” — Dorilian Lopez-Mago (2019).** DOI **10.1088/2040-8986/ab4c25**. **Primary fulltext read:** [arXiv:1906.05377](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.05377). | §3, Eqs. (12)–(17): explicit distinction between local DoP and DoP of integrated Stokes vector; global identity involving Stokes variances. §4: LG radial/azimuthal examples and Gouy-phase evolution. Quote: **“the global DoP is invariant under propagation through non-polarising optical elements”**. | **No.** Main invariant is global; examples assume spatially and temporally coherent light, hence local \(P=1\). Does not establish C8 for mixed covariance matrices. |
| **“Quantum theory of polarimetry: From quantum operations to Mueller matrices” — Aaron Z. Goldberg (2020).** DOI **10.1103/PhysRevResearch.2.023038**. **Primary fulltext read:** [arXiv:1912.01614](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.01614). | §§I.B, II, especially Eqs. (18)–(21), (27)–(35): Kraus/CPTP descriptions of Mueller transformations, including isotropic depolarization. Quote: **“We provide sets of quantum channels that underlie classical polarimetry and thus correspond to arbitrary Mueller matrices.”** | **Partly—optics/channel correspondence is prior art.** No LG radial Fresnel-response theorem, constant-purity-on-all-probes necessity, or arbitrary \(\Gamma_\pm\) split. Its broader quantum-polarimetry conjectures are not statements that C8 is open. |
| **“Topological rejection of noise by quantum skyrmions” — Pedro Ornelas, Isaac Nape, Robert de Mello Koch, Andrew Forbes (2025; preprint 2024).** DOI **10.1038/s41467-025-58232-4**. **Primary published fulltext read:** [Nature Communications](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-58232-4). | Results, “Quantum skyrmions”/“Topological protection,” Eqs. (1)–(4), Fig. 2: two-photon LG-OAM/polarization state, \(|\ell_1|\ne|\ell_2|\), mixed with \(I_4/4\); conditional spatial Stokes geometry. Quote: **“the change of state purity due to noise is a sphere of diminishing size”**. | **Partly—the closest purity/LG crossover.** Assumes a particular isotropic-noise family and studies normalized topological observables. Not C8’s same-\(|m|\), two-radial-order rotationally invariant sector class; no all-\(z\) necessity or classification of every PSD split. |
| **“Coherence, entanglement, and complementarity in mixed classical light” — Asma Al-Qasimi (2020).** DOI **10.1364/JOSAA.395172**. **Primary publisher-deposited abstract read:** [DOI record](https://doi.org/10.1364/JOSAA.395172); fulltext unavailable. | Abstract explicitly restricts to a one-parameter mixed-state model and polarization/nonseparability complementarity. Quote: **“for a specific model of mixed states, where the purity is determined by a single parameter”**. | **No established entailment; fulltext unresolved.** The accessible claim is model-specific, not complete local-\(P\)/Fresnel necessity. Do not advertise it as a Werner-family classification without reading the manuscript. |

## Inaccessible / bounded-out leads

- **OAM-resolved polarization in random light beams**, Pokharel–Raveh–Korotkova (2023), [10.1364/OL.496266](https://doi.org/10.1364/OL.496266): abstract read; fulltext not obtained.
- **Radial similarity measures for vectorial structured light**, Ochsner–Laatikainen–Korotkova (2026), [10.1364/OL.577164](https://doi.org/10.1364/OL.577164): abstract only; [NSF record](https://par.nsf.gov/biblio/10663359) explicitly embargoed until January 1, 2027.
- **Mueller matrices and the degree of polarization**, Lu–Chipman (1998), [10.1016/S0030-4018(97)00554-3](https://experts.azregents.edu/en/publications/mueller-matrices-and-the-degree-of-polarization/): institutional abstract read; fulltext unavailable. Relevant sphere-to-ellipsoid background, not an evidenced Fresnel bridge.
- Parent’s **OE.453631** and **OE.27.030044**: abstracts concern intensity/coherence-profile construction and evolution; no C8 theorem established. **JPHOT.2021.3103065**: publisher PDF returned HTTP 418; substantive scope unverified.
- **10.1117/12.3095057** (2026 underwater invariance): metadata only; publisher blocked. Al-Qasimi fulltext remains unavailable.

## Bounded search log / limits

Searched author/invariance combinations and exact crossovers including `"constant output purity" polarization`, `"constant purity" Fresnel`, `"depolarizing" Gouy`, `"qubit channel" Gouy/Fresnel`, `"transpose-depolarizing" polarization`, `"Laguerre-Gaussian" "block-diagonal"`, Werner/classical-light/spatial-mode combinations, and `"polarization invariance" "open problem"`. Inspected Cai-group author publications, Korotkova’s 2025 institutional bibliography and NSF’s newer records; Ostrovsky-name searches principally led to scalar coherent-mode constructions.

**No located source combines the complete constant-output-purity classification with C8’s radial Fresnel probe and sector-sum necessity. This is a bounded retrieval result—not proof that such literature does not exist.** No files changed or verification scripts executed.
